questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which finding pattern most directly reflects marrow failure in acute leukemia?
choices: Hypertension, bradycardia, and hyperreflexia
Fever, fatigue, petechiae, and low effective blood-cell production
Isolated ankle edema after standing
Painless jaundice with clay-colored stool
questions.explanation: Marrow replacement can reduce normal neutrophil, red-cell, and platelet production, leading to infection risk, anemia symptoms, and bruising or bleeding.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which cluster is most characteristic of lymphoma B symptoms?
choices: Fever, drenching night sweats, and unintentional weight loss
Polyuria, polydipsia, and fruity breath
Hematuria, flank pain, and dysuria
Tremor, heat intolerance, and exophthalmos
questions.explanation: Fever, drenching night sweats, and unintentional weight loss are systemic B symptoms. They are not diagnostic by themselves and require evaluation in context.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient has bone pain, anemia, elevated calcium, and worsening kidney function. Which disease pattern should the RN recognize?
choices: An isolated lymph-node infection
A multiple myeloma CRAB organ-injury pattern
Uncomplicated iron deficiency alone
Stable chronic venous insufficiency
questions.explanation: Hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction, anemia, and bone lesions form the CRAB pattern associated with symptomatic plasma-cell disease.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which patient requires the most urgent escalation?
choices: A patient with stable fatigue awaiting a scheduled clinic visit
A patient with a small painless node and no systemic symptoms
A patient with a very high blast count who develops dyspnea and new confusion
A patient with chronic back soreness unchanged for one year
questions.explanation: Respiratory or neurologic deterioration with a very high circulating blast burden can represent leukostasis or another emergency and requires immediate specialist evaluation and support.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which action is safest for a patient with suspected myeloma bone lesions and new hip pain?
choices: Perform forceful range-of-motion exercises
Encourage unassisted walking to test the bone
Use fall and bone precautions and promptly report the new focal pain
Massage directly over the painful area
questions.explanation: Myeloma can weaken bone and cause pathologic fracture. Protect the patient, support safe mobility, and arrange prompt assessment rather than stressing the painful site.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Why is tissue biopsy important when lymphoma is suspected?
choices: Node size alone establishes the exact subtype
Tissue architecture and cell features help establish the diagnosis and guide subtype-specific treatment
A biopsy eliminates the need for all staging
Biopsy is used only to measure electrolyte levels
questions.explanation: Lymphoma classification depends on tissue and cellular features. Imaging and other studies then define distribution and clinical context.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient with paraproteinemia develops headache, blurred vision, somnolence, and mucosal oozing. What is the priority concern?
choices: Possible hyperviscosity syndrome
Expected treatment fatigue only
Simple dehydration that can wait until tomorrow
An uncomplicated local skin reaction
questions.explanation: Neurologic, visual, cardiopulmonary, or bleeding findings with excess monoclonal protein can signal hyperviscosity and require urgent escalation and specialist-directed treatment.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient with possible multiple myeloma has confusion, weakness, calcium elevation, rising creatinine, and low urine output. What should the RN do?
choices: Treat constipation alone and reassess next week
Encourage unrestricted fluid regardless of cardiac status
Urgently notify the team, institute safety precautions, and begin ordered individualized monitoring and treatment
Wait for a fracture before limiting unassisted activity
questions.explanation: The cluster suggests severe hypercalcemia with kidney injury. Immediate escalation, neurologic and fluid assessment, fall protection, and prescribed therapy are required; fluids must reflect cardiac and renal reserve.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which symptom in a patient with lymphoma suggests a compressive emergency?
choices: Facial swelling, neck-vein distention, dyspnea, and difficulty lying flat
A stable appetite and normal breathing
An old healed incision
Mild thirst after exercise
questions.explanation: This pattern can indicate mediastinal or superior vena cava obstruction and warrants urgent airway, positioning, and oncology evaluation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which trend best demonstrates improvement after treatment for myeloma-associated hypercalcemia and kidney injury?
choices: Increasing confusion with falling urine output
Lower calcium with improving cognition, urine output, and creatinine trend
Less constipation but worsening weakness and rhythm change
Stable pain with new bladder dysfunction
questions.explanation: Improvement should include both laboratory and clinical recovery: calcium and kidney function trend toward the target while cognition, strength, hydration, and urine output improve.
